parts.note: to black a firm or its goods is to boycott them, a trade-union usage
to jack a car up is to raise it

explanation.surface: Cricketer Geoffrey Boycott sets out to lift the standard of the game.
explanation.walkthrough: Boycott looks like the Yorkshire cricketer's name, but it is a verb here: unions 'black' a firm they boycott.
explanation.definitionFit: Pontoon-style card play where players aim for twenty-one goes by this name.

indicators.note: the fish word goes around the letter for unit

parts.note: bass is a fish
I is the Roman numeral for one, a unit

explanation.surface: Fish swimming round a single unit as a means of support.
explanation.definitionFit: A foundation or underlying base is what supports something.

clue.text: Run into a crazy sick old animal

indicators.note: the run letter is put into the phrase a crazy

parts.note: mad means crazy
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
ill means sick

explanation.surface: Someone bumps into a mad, ailing old creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The armoured burrowing mammal of the Americas is a creature, hence an animal.

clue.text: Give up one sort of sparring for another

parts.note: to kick a habit is to give it up
boxing is another sort of sparring, standing in for the defining phrase

explanation.surface: Someone abandons one form of fighting practice and takes up a different one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' points back to 'sort of sparring': BOXING is another sort of sparring.
explanation.definitionFit: A combat sport combining punches and kicks is a form of sparring.

explanation.surface: An order to rise from bed, followed by a jibe at dull folk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get up' is a noun here, an outfit: anoraks are hooded waterproof jackets, and in British slang anoraks are obsessive, dull enthusiasts.
explanation.definitionFit: Hooded waterproof jackets are clothing, an outfit; obsessive nerdy enthusiasts are dull people in British slang.

indicators.note: within says the answer sits inside the words seeking domination

explanation.surface: A ruler seeks power over his whole realm.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm ruled by a monarch is a state or empire.

clue.text: … courage to get runs in passion

indicators.note: the runs abbreviation is placed inside the word for passion

parts.note: heat is strong feeling, as in the heat of the moment
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A batsman summons nerve to score runs in a fit of passion.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with spirit and bravery is said to have plenty of this, as in 'take this'.

indicators.note: heartlessly means the central letter of the word is removed

parts.note: heard means listened to

explanation.surface: An audience paid attention but felt nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The common mass of people, following others, is likened to a herd of cattle.

indicators.note: half here takes the second half of the letters of trap

parts.note: hid means concealed

explanation.surface: An insect is lured into a trap that is partly hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenfly and blackfly are common names for these sap-sucking insects.

clue.text: Dump truck on a railway town…

parts.note: a tipper is a lorry that tips its load, a dump truck

explanation.surface: A dumper lorry sits on a railway line by a town.
explanation.walkthrough: TIPPERARY is a town in Ireland, famous from the song 'It's a Long Way to Tipperary'.
explanation.definitionFit: An Irish market town gives its name to a county and to a First World War marching song.

parts.note: a sum is a total
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Someone departs, having scored a full century.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' reads as a verb (departs) but is the definition: the dried, ground leaves of this shrub are sold as a spice.
explanation.definitionFit: The shrub's dried foliage and berries are used for tanning and as a tart Middle Eastern spice.

clue.text: … for heartless spinner who lost title

indicators.note: being lost suggests the letters have gone astray and must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: losing its heart means the centre letter of spinner is dropped

explanation.surface: A bowler who no longer spins the ball well has been stripped of his championship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes the middle N of SPINNER, leaving SPINER; with WHO that pool is rearranged, signalled by 'lost'. 'title' is legal title to property, not a championship.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal title to something is the right of possession, the state of owning it.

explanation.surface: A one-word clue for people who cut hair.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the word: 'Hair' and 'dressers' are two separate definitions. SIDEBOARDS is a British word for side-whiskers (sideburns) and also for dresser-like dining-room cabinets.
explanation.definitionFit: Side-whiskers grown down the cheeks, and long low dining-room cupboards for crockery, share the one name.

indicators.note: discovered in the sense of uncovered: the answer is revealed within the words afraid, lest

explanation.surface: A worker is afraid of being caught slacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lazing about and not working is inactive or unoccupied.

clue.text: … trains crash and chap gets bitter

indicators.note: a crash wrecks the trains, so their letters are jumbled

parts.note: a gent is a chap

explanation.surface: After a train crash a man grows resentful.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp, harsh and biting in taste or tone, as acerbic remarks are.

clue.text: About 50 cuts, then takes it easy

parts.note: re means about or concerning
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
axes are cuts, as in budget cuts

explanation.surface: After making about fifty job cuts, a boss relaxes.
explanation.definitionFit: To unwind or rest is to stop working hard and loosen up.

clue.text: Returned new dresser found outside, for example

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are placed outside the abbreviation for example
new signals the letters of dresser are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A newly bought dresser is left outside, for instance.
explanation.definitionFit: To go back to an earlier state is to revert.

clue.text: A blemish in mother's make up…

indicators.note: A plus the blemish word is placed inside the word for mother

parts.note: ma is mother
a scar is a blemish on the skin

explanation.surface: A mark on the face is hidden by mum's cosmetics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make up' is the noun, cosmetics, of which mascara is one.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyelash colouring is one kind of cosmetic, so it is an example of facial cosmetics.

indicators.note: the shortened increase word goes inside the shock word

parts.note: to appal is to shock

indicators.note: curtailed means having its tail, the last letter, cut off

parts.note: a raise is an increase in pay

explanation.surface: A pay rise cut back comes as a shock at the annual staff review.
explanation.definitionFit: An assessment or evaluation of performance is a review.

explanation.surface: Asking what the motive for a cup of coffee is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reason' gives grounds as in grounds for complaint; coffee grounds are the dregs left in the pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A basis or justification is one sense; the used particles left after brewing coffee are the other.

explanation.surface: Someone half-recognises a detective.
explanation.walkthrough: Spotted dick is a British steamed suet pudding with currants; 'Dick' is not a detective here. 'saw' means noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: A currant-studded pudding is a kind of 'dick'; and noticed or caught sight of is the other sense.

clue.text: Untidy ditch by the outskirts of Pudsey

parts.note: to scrap something is to ditch it

indicators.note: the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A messy ditch beside the edge of Pudsey, a town near Leeds in Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Something disorganised or messy, made of bits and pieces, is careless and untidy.

parts.note: reads like a girl named Hazel, but hazel is a tree, and a young one is meant

explanation.surface: Perhaps a little girl called Hazel.
explanation.definitionFit: A juvenile tree, such as a young hazel, is called this.

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: A hesitant person finally decides to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word for therefore is used in English to mean consequently.

indicators.note: sort as a verb means arrange, so the letters are re-sorted

explanation.surface: A gaze that seems somewhat royal.
explanation.definitionFit: A fierce stare is a hostile look.

clue.text: Make allowance in case men opt for cooking…

indicators.note: cooking signals that these letters are mixed up as ingredients are

explanation.surface: In this situation men choose to do the cooking, so allowances must be made.
explanation.definitionFit: To offset or make up for something is to make amends or counterbalance it.

clue.text: Yet someone started giving the odds…

parts.note: even means yet, as in even better

indicators.note: started means the word's opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: Even so, someone began quoting betting prices.
explanation.definitionFit: Betting at one-to-one, where a win doubles the stake, is a price in gambling.

clue.text: … the pretence would fall short of disgrace

indicators.note: falling short means the word stops before its last letter

parts.note: shame is disgrace

explanation.surface: Putting on an act would not quite amount to disgrace.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoax or false show is a counterfeit, a mere front.

explanation.surface: Describing a cowboy-film meal.
explanation.walkthrough: A spaghetti western is a cowboy film made in Italy, so the answer describes a kind of western as well as being a pasta.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian-made cowboy films are named after the long thin pasta, which is also an everyday dish.

clue.text: Result of being seen around university…

indicators.note: around in the sense of scattered about tells us to mix the letters

explanation.surface: Consequences of being spotted on campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Result' is a verb here: to follow on as a consequence.
explanation.definitionFit: To follow as a consequence is to come after something as its outcome.

indicators.note: first picks only the opening letter of degree

parts.note: a ream is a quantity of paper, five hundred sheets

explanation.surface: A student pictures getting a first-class degree on paper.
explanation.definitionFit: To fantasise or picture something in the mind is to conjure it up.

clue.text: Drug? Understand one has a list compiled

I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: compiled suggests the letters are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone grasps that a list of drugs has been drawn up.
